claims.text: Confirm with multiple readings; home BP measurement helps confirm the diagnosis.
claims.quote: Multiple measurements of BP are needed to confirm hypertension because of the inherent variability of blood pressure. Blood pressure typically fluctuates with time of day; in classic diurnal variation, BP is higher by day (especially in the morning) and lower by night. Home blood pressure measurement, using a cuffed device, can help confirm a diagnosis of hypertension

claims.text: Home or ambulatory monitoring when white coat or masked hypertension is suspected.
claims.quote: Home or ambulatory BP monitoring is indicated when white coat hypertension or masked hypertension is suspected.

claims.text: Newly diagnosed: urinalysis, spot urine albumin:creatinine ratio, creatinine, potassium, sodium, calcium, fasting glucose, lipid panel, TSH, and ECG.
claims.quote: When hypertension is newly diagnosed, do a urinalysis, spot urine albumin:creatinine ratio, blood tests (creatinine, potassium, sodium, calcium, fasting plasma glucose, lipid panel, and thyroid-stimulating hormone), and ECG.

claims.text: Renal ultrasound if urinalysis shows albuminuria, casts or microhematuria, or creatinine or cystatin C is high.
claims.quote: Renal ultrasound to evaluate kidney size may provide useful information if urinalysis detects albuminuria (proteinuria), casts, or microhematuria, or if serum creatinine or cystatin C is elevated.

claims.text: Plasma aldosterone and renin activity for hypokalemia not due to diuretics; also screen for primary aldosteronism in resistant hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea or early stroke.
claims.quote: Patients with hypokalemia unrelated to diuretic use are evaluated for high salt intake and for primary aldosteronism by measuring plasma aldosterone levels and plasma renin activity. Screening for primary aldosteronism is also recommended for patients with resistant hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea, or early stroke

claims.text: ECG: a broad, notched P wave is an early sign of hypertensive heart disease; high QRS voltage means LVH, often followed by echocardiography.
claims.quote: On ECG, a broad, notched P-wave indicates atrial hypertrophy and, although nonspecific, may be one of the earliest signs of hypertensive heart disease. Elevated QRS voltage, with or without evidence of ischemia, may occur later and indicates left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). When LVH is seen on ECG, echocardiography is often done.

claims.text: Labile, high BP with headache, palpitations, sweating, tremor or pallor: plasma free metanephrines for pheochromocytoma and TSH for hyperthyroidism.
claims.quote: Patients with labile, significantly elevated BP and symptoms such as headache, palpitations, tachycardia, excessive perspiration, tremor, and pallor are screened for pheochromocytoma by measuring plasma free metanephrines and for hyperthyroidism, first by measuring thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH).
